# SafeFQL

> SafeFQL (Safe Flow Q-Learning) is a state-of-the-art method for offline safe
> reinforcement learning. It combines a Hamilton-Jacobi reachability-based
> safety critic, trained via a max-backup Bellman recursion, with a one-step
> flow policy distilled from a flow-matching behavior model. This enforces
> hard, state-wise safety constraints at deployment with a single forward
> pass and no rejection sampling.

## Key facts

- Full name: Safe Flow Q-Learning (SafeFQL)
- Authors: Mumuksh Tayal, Manan Tayal (equal contribution), Ravi Prakash
- Affiliation: Indian Institute of Science (IISc), India
- Venue: Reinforcement Learning Conference (RLC) 2026; Reinforcement Learning
  Journal, Volume 7, 2026
- Problem area: offline safe reinforcement learning / safe RL / constrained RL
- Core idea: a Hamilton-Jacobi reachability-based safety critic gates a
  distilled one-step flow policy, replacing both expected-cost Lagrangian
  methods and rejection-sampled safe generative policies (e.g. FISOR,
  SafeIFQL)
- Headline results: lowest constraint-violation rate across all evaluated
  benchmarks (Safe Boat Navigation, Safety Gymnasium velocity-constrained
  tasks), reward competitive with or exceeding prior safe generative
  baselines, at roughly 2.5x lower inference latency and no rejection
  sampling

## Links

- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15136

- Offline dataset (Point Robot / Boat Robot): https://huggingface.co/datasets/tayalmanan/SafeBoatData
